properties.headline: Wildfire with IMMEDIATE EVACUATION for the west side of Atoka Reservoir.
properties.description: At 1715  a large and destructive wildfire was burning out of control north of Atoka  spreading rapidly north along the west side of the Atoka Reservoir. Wildfires can damage or destroy structures and can harm or kill people and animals. For your safety  EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY to the northwest toward Lehigh.
properties.instruction: Those between Highway 69 and East Tower Road and North Coal Creek Road should LEAVE this area NOW to avoid injury or death. Do not delay to pack belongings. Evacuate towards the northwest to Lehigh. Roads in the area may be impacted by fire and smoke. Never drive into heavy smoke. SLOW DOWN & MOVE OVER for emergency vehicles.

CMAMtext: Atoka Co EM: EVACUATION ORDER for north Atoka due to a wildfire. LEAVE NOW toward Lehigh
CMAMlongtext: Atoka Co EM: A dangerous wildfire is located north of Atoka, spreading rapidly west. This area is in IMMEDIATE DANGER from wildfires which can cause injury/death, burn down homes/other structures. LEAVE NOW toward the northwest toward Lehigh. Do not delay to pack belongings. Never drive into heavy smoke.

miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

Do not enter or cross flowing water or water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 1:40PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.Elevated water levels are expected along the river over the next
several days due to recent heavy rainfall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.
